title: Légal's mate
line: A queen given up so that the minor pieces mate.

steps.text: Black's bishop attacks your knight, and your queen stands behind it. If the knight moves, the bishop can take the queen.
Take the pawn in the center with the knight anyway, and leave your queen to the bishop.
steps.hint: The knight jumps to the pawn that stands in front of Black's pawns.
steps.after: Black takes the queen. Now see what your other pieces can do.

steps.text: You are a queen down, but Black's king is open. Capture the pawn beside it with your bishop, with check.
steps.hint: The bishop takes on the diagonal toward the king. The knight guards it there.
steps.after: The king has one square to go to.

steps.hint: The knight jumps to the center, next to the king's last squares.
steps.after: Légal's mate. Two knights and a bishop mate, while Black's bishop sits on your queen's square.

steps.text: Now you are Black, right after the knight took the pawn. Do not take the queen. Take the knight.

also.g4e6: That avoids the mate too. This lesson takes the knight.

wrong.g4d1: Then the bishop takes on f7 with check, and the other knight mates on d5.

steps.hint: A pawn can take the knight in the center.
steps.after: The queen can take your bishop, and White is a pawn up, but there is no mate.

summary: Giving up the queen can pay when the minor pieces mate. When a queen is offered for free, look for the trap.
